visible.presentation_text:
Consult request from the facility's licensed wildlife rehabilitator.

Eastern box turtle, adult, estimated 25–40 years old. Surrendered by a family who kept it in a backyard pen for two years after finding it during a move.

Presented with severe ulcerative shell disease with full-thickness carapace lesions, underlying bone involvement on radiographs, and osteomyelitis extending to the vertebral column. Blood work shows marked leukocytosis and severe anemia. Cultures grew mixed gram-negative organisms; six weeks of directed therapy with debridement has produced continued extension of the lesions.

Animal has not fed voluntarily in three weeks, is losing condition, and is minimally responsive to stimulation. Attending veterinarian assesses the process as advanced, unresponsive to treatment, and expects continued deterioration; reptile pain is poorly characterized behaviorally but the extent of the disease is consistent with substantial ongoing nociceptive input.

Animal is non-releasable. Eastern box turtles show strong site fidelity to a home range of a few hectares; individuals released outside their home range wander persistently, show elevated mortality, and can introduce pathogens into naive populations. Release at an unknown or approximate origin is not supported. Massachusetts prohibits relocation of wildlife.

Placement: box turtles are common in captivity and in the surrendered-pet stream; the two regional facilities contacted have no capacity and report frequent similar surrenders. No breeding program applies to a wild-origin animal of unknown provenance. No research use.

Permanent captivity for this animal means an indoor and outdoor enclosure with thermal gradient, seasonal management including brumation, and daily care for a plausible 40 to 60 further years. This animal will likely outlive the facility's current staff.
menu_options: Continue holding while placement is sought
Place the animal with the surrendering family under a captive-wildlife arrangement
Release the animal at the approximate corridor described
Transfer the animal to another facility
